title: Unify contrast-driven tokens and elevation matrix for component library
creator: Maya Chen
description: Rethink and consolidate color tokens, typography scale, spacing/radius, and shadow/elevation tokens into a contrast-first token set and a composable elevation matrix. Goal is to reduce visual regressions across Buttons, Tables, Charts and Cards while improving accessibility and making runtime token mapping predictable for Dedicated/Private deployments.
impact_summary: A unified token scheme will affect all core components (Buttons, Tables, Charts, Inputs, Cards, Modals). Expected benefits: consistent cross-theme contrast, fewer one-off overrides, simpler runtime mapping for dark/light and high-contrast modes, and clearer migration path for engineering. Risk: temporary visual drift for edge-case components and potential subtle spacing regressions in legacy layouts.
proposal_summary: Introduce a two-layer token system: (1) Contrast tokens keyed by role (bg-container, fg-primary, border-muted) with explicit WCAG contrast ratio metadata; (2) Elevation matrix tokens representing layered surfaces with both shadow (x/y/blur/alpha) and elevation color overlay tokens. Add a 12-step typographic scale with variable-font fallback and a 4-step modular spacing/radius scale. Create automated lint rules to flag components that reference legacy tokens.
migration_plan: Create a mapping table from legacy tokens to new role-based tokens (design + engineering);
Implement a runtime shim in the design tokens package to expose both old and new keys for 2 release cycles;
Update top-priority components (Buttons, Tables, Charts) in a canary branch and ship visuals to staging;
Run visual diffs against baseline snapshots and iterate until delta < 1% for primary screens;
Deprecate legacy tokens and remove after two cycles with documented codemods for client SDKs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Design token spec published + Figma libraries updated (1 week)
Phase 2: Engine changes + shim release (ENG-4122) + PRD signoff (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Component updates for Buttons/Tables/Charts on staging, run snapshots (1 week)
Phase 4: Expand to lower-priority components, monitor Console metrics for visual regressions and customer-reported issues (2 weeks)
Phase 5: Remove shim and legacy tokens after no regressions for 2 cycles
acceptance_criteria: All primary components render with new tokens in light/dark/high-contrast without layout shifts > 4px
Automated visual-diff coverage for top 50 flows with <1% pixel delta on staging
Contrast report demonstrates WCAG AA compliance for all text sizes and WCAG AAA for large text where applicable
Codebase contains codemods and migration docs; no remaining direct references to legacy tokens in main branch after removal snapshot
qa_checklist: Run visual diff harness for Chrome/Firefox on desktop and mobile widths
Verify color contrast ratios using automated tools and manual spot checks
Check shadow/elevation consistency across z-index changes
Validate spacing tokens in responsive containers and tables
Confirm typography scale fallback works on Windows and macOS system fonts
decisions: Adopt role-based contrast tokens instead of semantic color names to reduce accidental misuse
Elevation will be two-dimensional: a shadow spec and an optional color overlay for tinted surfaces
Typography scale will switch to variable fonts with a fixed fallback stack for environments that don't support variable fonts
tradeoffs: Variable-font-first approach improves runtime flexibility but may introduce rendering differences on older platforms
Keeping a runtime shim increases maintenance window but reduces customer breakage during rollout
Stricter contrast thresholds may reduce palette vibrancy and require additional designer approvals
